newsitem.title: GERMANY: British army vehicle runs into striking Germans.
newsitem.headline: British army vehicle runs into striking Germans.

text.p: Three German civilian workers on strike outside a British army base were slightly injured on Thursday when a British soldier tried to drive a vehicle through a line of pickets, union leaders said.

But accounts of the seriousness of the accident, which happened outside British army barracks in the North Rhine-Westphalian town of Herford, differed as widely as the positions of the workers and army management in a dispute over the impact of cost-cutting measures at the bases.

While German public sector trade union OeTV said three strikers had to be taken to hospital after a British soldier accelerated into a group of protesting workers, a British army spokeswoman said just one man had been hit.
She added the worker had sustained a bruise to his left leg. The full German police report on the matter had not yet been filed, she said.

The OeTV union, one of Germany's most powerful, said it had received what it was viewing as a written apology from a senior British officer over the incident but that charges were still to be pressed.
In the letter sent to the OeTV, the army's civilian administration office said it was sorry to hear about the incident but that further action should await the result of the German police's enquiry.
The British army spokeswoman said the soldier, who was not named, would be questioned by military police as part of their enquiry.

The accident happened as more than 3,000 civilians, mainly Germans, went on strike for the fourth day in protest at cost-saving measures they say are threatening thousands of jobs among the 35,000 staff employed by the allies in Germany.
Many civilians employed at the bases have already seen their jobs go as forces in Germany, especially American troops, have been reduced since the end of the Cold War.
